attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed Substack post, not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: Calling the prospect 'bonkers' is an unhedged dismissal, a firm expectation that perfectly reliable, hallucination-free chatbots would not exist within a year. The surrounding hedges ('very likely') attach to other sentences. The literal threshold and the one-year horizon are preserved.

contract.note: The literal reading of 'perfectly reliable, hallucination-free' uses the speaker's own words, and the 23 Feb 2025 deadline follows from the post date. Using the best model on an independent benchmark as the test is a fair proxy for a universal negative.

evidence.note: Independent leaderboard, updated 28 Feb 2025, days after the deadline. The best model scored 0.7% hallucination and every listed model was above zero. It covers summarization only, but that is a favorable setting, so it still shows that no tested model was hallucination-free.

output.rationale: The deadline (about 23 Feb 2025) has passed. Vectara's independent leaderboard from 28 Feb 2025 shows nonzero hallucination rates for every leading model, including the best at 0.7%. No evidence in the packet shows any chatbot at zero. This meets the support condition. The limit is that the test covers summarization only.
